title: xargs
subtitle: Turn stdin words into command arguments — flip to reveal meaning

cards.meaning: Reads arguments from stdin (split on blank spaces or newlines) and runs a command using that input as the command’s arguments
cards.notes: Other half of find: find prints paths, xargs turns lines into arguments

cards.meaning: If you omit a command, the default is /bin/echo
cards.notes: Multiline input becomes a single echoed line

cards.meaning: One cmd with many extra args from stdin
cards.notes: Bare xargs cmd = many args on one command

cards.meaning: One touch per input item; {} is replaced once per item (not all names as extra args on one touch)
cards.notes: xargs -i cmd {} = one cmd per item

cards.meaning: Preferred modern GNU spelling of -i — replace-string mode, one command per item
Same as -i with {} but custom replace string T instead of {}
Input items terminated by a null byte instead of whitespace; quotes and backslashes are not special
cards.notes: Use when names may contain spaces, quotes, or backslashes. Pair with find -print0

cards.meaning: Print paths null-separated so they pair safely with xargs -0
cards.notes: Spaces in filenames break default xargs

cards.meaning: Run up to max-procs processes at a time (default 1); can speed work on multicore
Run as many processes as possible at a time (no cap — be careful)
